title: Foundations of Sociological Thought
sources_used: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain Herbert Spencer’s contribution to evolutionary sociology. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Herbert Spencer applied Darwin’s theory of evolution to society,
  • explaining progress through adaptation. His ideas formed the basis of
  • social evolutionism and differentiation. [U] / [CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the concept of structural-functionalism. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Structural- functionalism sees society as a structure of interrelated parts
  • functioning to maintain equilibrium and stability among social
  • institutions. [U] / [CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the phrase 'survival of the fittest' as coined by Spencer. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• ‘Survival of the fittest’ means that only adaptable individuals or societies
  • progress, linking biological evolution with social development. [U] /
  • [CO2)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Mention one feature of Spencer’s industrial society. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• [U] / [CO2] Industrial society is characterized by voluntary cooperation,
  • specialization of labour, and contract-based relationships replacing
  • status-based ties.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Do you agree that economy determines all aspects of life? Justify with an example / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• [E] / [CO3] Economy determines all life aspects because material
  • conditions influence ideas, politics, and culture, as argued by Marx in
  • historical materialism.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: State one difference between dialectics and metaphysics. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• [U] / [CO3] Dialectics stresses contradictions and social change, while
  • metaphysics focuses on static, abstract reasoning detached from material
  • reality.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Define 'social facts' according to Durkheim. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• [K] / [CO3] Durkheim defines ‘social facts’ as external, coercive norms
  • that exist independently and constrain individual actions.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: List the four types of suicide identified by Durkheim. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• [K] / [CO3] Durkheim’s four types of suicide are egoistic, altruistic,
  • anomic, and fatalistic—each linked to varying social integration levels.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain one use and one limitation of ideal types in sociology. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• [E] / [CO3] Ideal types provide conceptual clarity for comparison, but
  • they are subjective and lack empirical accuracy.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the concept of totemism in Durkheim’s study of religion. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• [U] / [CO3] Totemism, according to Durkheim, represents the worship of
  • social symbols that embody collective consciousness.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Differentiate between functionalism and conflict perspectives. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• [An] / [CO1] Functionalism emphasizes order and consensus; conflict
  • theory highlights power struggles and social inequality.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Differentiate between military and industrial societies described by Spencer. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• [An] / [CO2] Military societies rely on compulsion and hierarchy, whereas
  • industrial societies encourage cooperation and freedom.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Give one example of a micro-sociological theory. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• [A] / [CO4] Symbolic Interactionism is a micro theory that studies how
  • individuals construct meanings through social interactions.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Illustrate historical materialism using the Industrial Revolution. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• [A] / [CO3] Historical materialism illustrates that economic
  • transformations, like the Industrial Revolution, reshape social relations
  • and class structures.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Define the term 'super-organism' in sociology. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• [K] / [CO2] A super-organism refers to society functioning as an
  • organism, with interdependent structures maintaining social order.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Define 'social solidarity'. / [CO3] [2x13 = 26]
questions.solution_html:
• [K] / [CO3] Social solidarity denotes unity achieved through shared
  • norms, values, and social integration among members.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
